gen-gf-gabarito-gf-yuji-syuku: Gabarito draws its letters like bent wire, one nib, no thick-to-thin shifts. Yuji Syuku, a classic serif with open spacing and curves that stop before turning inward, gives a longer text a dignified, unhurried pace.
gen-gf-gabarito-ibm-plex-serif: Expressive Gabarito looks bent from a single wire, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. IBM Plex Serif follows in a text serif whose thick strokes are only slightly heavier than its thin ones, so paragraphs move along with a steady, corporate confidence.
gen-gf-gaegu-fs-bespoke-serif: Gaegu writes in a smooth marker-like line, inviting and graceful, as if one wire ran through the whole sentence. Bespoke Serif adds dignified thick and thin strokes beneath, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-cascadia-mono: Precise and structured, Geist Mono has a chunky, tall midzone and unclosed round letters. Cascadia Mono is the sans-serif underneath, with curves as thick as its stems, so a slightly smaller body size makes sense.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-julius-sans-one: Drifting, widely spaced letters with unclosed curves mark Geist Mono as the heading. And Julius Sans One adds a plain sans with big gaps between letters and capitals barely taller than lowercase, so the page feels light but orderly.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads wide and sturdy, with stubby ascenders next to a big x-height. Its uniform line and open curves sit well under the chunky, drifting letters of Geist Mono, which gives the pair a crisp, structured clarity.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga is a sans-serif with flat linework and ascenders that barely clear the x-height. Geist Mono above it brings chunky, tall midzones and unclosed round letters, and the generous tracking below lets each word breathe.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega has a one-nib look, with a visible gap in every c and a body nearly matching the capitals. And Geist Mono leads with its chunky, drifting letters, so a plain sans body at a modest size lets the heading stand out.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-lexend-peta: Geist Mono spaces its chunky, tall-midzone letters apart and leaves every small round letter generously unclosed. Lexend Peta, a plain sans, answers with wide-mouthed curves; the heading earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-geist-mono-gf-lexend-tera: Geist Mono sets precise, drifting letters with unclosed curves and a chunky, tall midzone. Lexend Tera, a sans with a plotter-pen line and letters spaced like stepping stones, makes a longer text feel open and contemporary.
